summary: Timeboxed, minimized netflow-headers-only extract for privacy-led compliance verification
description:
Issue summary:
A compliance request to verify that inference traffic for tenant T-4482 did not egress to unapproved 3rd-party networks during a suspected configuration change window (2026-03-03 03:00:00 to 2026-03-03 06:00:00 UTC). Team requests a minimized extract containing only network flow headers (no payloads, no request/response bodies, no inference outputs) to demonstrate routing and external endpoints observed.

Impact:
Compliance needs evidence to close a customer data routing inquiry. Customer is enterprise tier and has flagged possible cross-region egress. Providing unminimized logs would expose customer IPs and internal hostnames; we must minimize to reduce privacy risk.

Environment:
Production (prod-us-east), VPCs and NAT gateway logs, load balancer flow logs, and router netflow samples for the tenant's dedicated subnets.

Requested data and minimization plan:
- Time window: 2026-03-03T03:00:00Z to 2026-03-03T06:00:00Z (3 hour slice)
- Scope: flows where source_tag contains tenant:T-4482 OR x-request-id associated with T-4482
- Fields to extract: timestamp, src_cidr (anonymized to /24), dst_cidr (external IPs hashed with salt), src_port (keep), dst_port (keep), protocol, bytes_sent, bytes_received, flow_direction, request_id (redacted to first 8 chars), egress_gateway_id, route_table_id
- Explicitly excluded: request/response bodies, inference outputs, HTTP headers beyond ports, SNI, full hostnames, complete IPs for external addresses
- Redaction rules: internal private IPs shown as /24 CIDR; external IPs one-way-hashed (SHA256 + team salt) and stored in a restricted bucket; last octet redacted for any internal hosts when hashing is not possible
- Retention and storage: single-use S3 bucket "redwood-compliance-temp/netflow/INT-82001", object-level encryption, lifecycle rule to delete after 14 days, access ACL restricted to Security, Compliance, and oncall SRE only.

Approval requested from: Security, Legal (data privacy), and Infra Oncall. Requesting timeboxed access path and an audit log of who downloads the artifact.

Reasoning/Justification:
Minimization reduces PII exposure while still providing the routing evidence Compliance requires. The extract is scoped to the tenant and a narrow time window to prevent unnecessary data exposure.

Next steps if approved:
1) SRE will run the netflow query with minimization and write to the temp bucket.
2) Security will verify redaction/hash process and approve the artifact for review.
3) Compliance will analyze the extract and close the customer inquiry or request further steps.

Business owner: Compliance (Lina Cohen). Technical contact: Marco Reyes (SRE).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Marco Reyes: Noted. I can run the netflow aggregation from the ELK ingest and NAT gateway logs. Need Security approval on hashing scheme and confirmation that request_id truncated to 8 chars is sufficient for correlation without exposing full identifiers.

2026-03-11 - Priya Kapoor (Security): Recommend: external IPs hashed with a per-ticket salt stored in Vault, keep first 8 chars of request_id, redact SNI/hostnames entirely. Also require that the temp S3 bucket is in the Redwood security account and has Object Lock disabled. I will need to review the query before export.

2026-03-11 - Lina Cohen (Compliance): Approve in principle if minimization steps are implemented exactly as listed. Compliance requests a separate checksum file listing the query used and hashes salt identifier (not the salt itself). We also want the retention policy set to auto-delete at 14 days.

2026-03-12 - Marco Reyes: Running a dry-run query against a 15-minute sample to validate fields. Found request_id normalized at ingestion as trace_id; mapping to tenant is via tenant_tag. Dry-run output contains internal hostnames in the egress_gateway_id field — planning to strip hostnames and keep only gateway IDs. Will attach dry-run sample (redacted) for Security review.

2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor (Security): Reviewed dry-run. Good progress. Two asks: 1) ensure salts are rotated per-ticket and recorded in Vault's audit log, 2) provide a short runbook of the extraction steps to be archived with the artifact. Once satisfied, I'll move my approval to 'approved for export'.
investigation_notes: Checked ELK indices: nat-gateway-flows-2026-03 and lb-access-2026-03 contain candidate records. Tenant tag present on ~98% of candidate flows.
Confirmed request_id mapping exists in request-metadata index; will join on first 8 chars after truncation for correlation checks.
Observed small set (~12) of flows with SNI populated; will redact SNI and full hostnames before export.
Estimated extracted file size after minimization: ~45 MB compressed for 3 hour window.
Access pattern: artifact creation requires a signed S3 presigned URL for download; all downloads will be logged to CloudTrail.
Risk assessment: Low to medium if redaction/hashing executed correctly. Failure mode: unhashed external IPs could expose PII. Mitigation: Security to verify hashes prior to release.
